title: Session cost resilience and contingency playbook
author: Maya Patel
body:
h1. Session cost resilience & contingency playbook

Short intro
This playbook documents pragmatic, production-ready approaches for protecting customer sessions and containment of token spend during sudden cost or capacity anomalies. It targets product managers, SREs, and platform engineers responsible for: hosted API tiers, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments. The goal is to ensure predictable customer experience while bounding spend and enabling rapid, safe rollback.

h2. Scope and audience
- Scope: session-scoped fallbacks, per-route cost throttles, emergency quantization and fidelity gates, and operational runbooks for switching contingency modes.
- Audience: product owners, runtime engineers, SRE oncall, support escalation leads, account success for large customers.

h2. Definitions and decision criteria
- Session: a stateful conversation or streaming transaction identified by session_id or tenant_route.
- Per-token cost anomaly: observed per-token billable cost for a model variant exceeds baseline by > 2x for rolling 10m.
- Capacity shock: sustained CPU/GPU utilization > 85% with increased 95th latency for > 5m.
- Fidelity degradation: deliberate change to model configuration (quantization, smaller variant, truncated context) intended to reduce cost/latency.

h2. High-level strategy
1. Detect: surface cost and latency signals at session granularity.
2. Contain: apply session-level policies (throttles, sampling, fidelity gates) to stop uncontrolled spend.
3. Protect UX: route to cheaper-compatible variant or enable graceful partial responses.
4. Restore & Analyze: roll metrics capture and run post-incident triage to refine thresholds.

h2. Contingency options (quick reference)
{panel}Use the table below to pick the fastest safe action. Include expected RTO, UX impact and unit-cost delta.{panel}
||Action||Typical RTO||UX impact||Cost delta (estimate)||Who owns||
|Emergency throttling (per-session token cap)|< 1 min|users see truncation on long replies|-30% to -70%|SRE / Runtime|
|Fallback routing to smaller variant (e.g. 8B -> 3B quantized)|~1–3 min|lower factuality/verbosity|-50% to -80%|Product + Runtime|
|Prefix/KV cache bypass (disable large-context heavy retrieval)|~2–5 min|some context lost; quicker response|-20% to -40%|Runtime|
|Adaptive streaming (shorter partial responses with resume token)|< 2 min|minor UX change; requires client support|-15% to -50%|Eng Dev / SDK|
|Billing soft-limit enforcement & customer notification|< 1 min|request rejected; clear error + email warning|direct spend cap|Finance + CS|

h2. Recommended default policies (global baseline)
- Per-session rolling token cap: 10,000 tokens per 24h window (start conservative; teams may adjust per-customer tier).
- Per-route cost shock guard: trigger when median per-token inference cost > 2x baseline for 10m.
- Fallback order (automated): 1) enable token cap, 2) route to quantized variant, 3) apply prefix drop, 4) throttle non-interactive routes.

h2. Monitoring signals & alerting (concrete examples)
- Metrics to track (session granularity): session_token_count, session_cost_estimate_usd, session_95_latency_ms, model_variant_reply_quality_score.
- Alert rules (examples):
  - Cost anomaly alert: WHEN max(session_cost_estimate_usd / session_expected_cost_usd) > 2 FOR 10m -> P1 to SRE and Product.
  - Capacity shock alert: WHEN avg(gpu_utilization{pool=\"dedicated\"}) > 85% FOR 5m AND p95(latency) > 1.5x baseline -> P0 oncall.
  - Degradation detection: WHEN rolling drift in reply_quality_score for a variant > 15% relative to baseline across 5% of requests -> create regression ticket and evaluate rollback.

Example PromQL-style queries (adapt to our telemetry pipeline):
- per-session token count (last 5m): sum(rate(session_token_count[5m])) by (session_id)
- session cost ratio: session_cost_estimate_usd / session_expected_cost_usd

h2. Operational runbook: emergency cost containment (step-by-step)
1. Triage: confirm alert and scope (affected routes/customers). Capture: tenant_id list, session_ids, model variants in use.
2. Apply fast containment: set per-session token cap (API call below) for affected tenant(s). Notify CS and affected customers with templated message.
3. If tokens continue to spike: flip automated fallback routing to smallest compatible quantized variant for affected routes.
4. Observe 10 minutes. If latency/cost improved, keep new route and initiate customer outreach. If UX regressions unacceptable, revert and prepare targeted throttles per-session.
5. Post-incident: run cost-impact analysis and update regression prompt sets for the variant any time fallback routing was triggered.

h3. Example CLI / API snippets
- Temporarily set per-session token cap (admin CLI):
{code}
redwood admin set-token-cap --tenant-id=acme-inc --session-window=24h --max-tokens=5000
{code}
- Emergency route policy (JSON payload for route service) – apply to a route:
{code}
{
  "route_id": "tenant/acme-inc/route/chat",
  "fallback_order": ["quantized-3b", "trimmed-13b-quant"],
  "behavior": {
    "max_tokens_per_session": 5000,
    "sampling_rate": 1.0
  },
  "reason": "emergency-cost-containment-2026-04-29",
  "ttl": "2h"
}
{code}
Note: above is an operational payload applied through the internal route-management API. Use the admin UI when possible to ensure audit logging.

h2. Compatibility matrix and UX tradeoffs (short table)
||Action||Latency impact||Expected quality impact||When to use||
|Fallback to smaller quantized variant|lower latency (-20% to -50%)|quality varies: hallucination risk ↑|capacity cost shock; immediate budget containment|
|Token-cap per session|no latency change|truncation of long flows|unexpected runaways or abusive scripts|
|Prefix drop / retrieval bypass|latency ↓ somewhat|loss of context; may reduce accuracy|heavy retrieval-driven workloads|

h2. Testing and rollout checklist
- Automated chaos tests: simulate token runaway with synthetic sessions; verify fallback triggers and audit logs.
- Customer sandboxing: run canary with 5% of traffic for a week before enabling auto-fallback for a customer.
- UX validation: run A/B on trimmed responses to ensure critical flows still succeed (search, code completion, legal summary).
- Billing simulation: run billing reconciliation for sample tenant under fallback scenarios to estimate downstream revenue impact.

h2. Governance & change management
- Any new automated fallback rule requires: product sign-off, SRE runbook update, and a scheduled postmortem if triggered in production.
- Emergency changes must be recorded in the incident timeline and converted to a change request if retained beyond 24 hours.

h2. Ownership and escalation
- Primary: Runtime engineering (oncall flips containment toggles).
- Secondary: Product (approve customer-facing messages and permanent policy changes).
- Tertiary: Finance & CS (billing impacts, refunds, or credits).
- Escalation path: oncall -> runtime lead -> SRE manager -> head of product.

h2. Post-incident analysis template (to be filled out within 72h)
1. Incident summary (impact, timeframe).
2. Root cause hypothesis and evidence.
3. Actions taken (containment steps and why).
4. Customer impact list and communication timeline.
5. Cost delta analysis (actual vs expected).
6. Follow-ups and owners (code/config changes, alert tuning, SLA changes).

h2. Example customer communication (templated)
Subject: Temporary service adjustment for [product/route] on [date]
Body: We detected an operational issue that increased model serving costs and risked degraded performance. We temporarily applied protective controls (token caps/fallback routing) to maintain service availability. We are reviewing the incident and will follow up with a detailed timeline and remediation plan. Contact: customer-success@redwood.ai

h2. Appendix: rollout timeline for automated fallback feature (quarter plan)
- Week 1–2: Instrumentation and unit tests (runtime team).
- Week 3–4: Chaos experiments and telemetry dashboards (SRE + Observability).
- Week 5: Customer canary with opt-in pilot (1–3 customers).
- Week 6–8: Expand to tiered rollout (5%, 25%, 100%) with monitoring gates.
- Post rollout: 90-day review and SLA adjustment if necessary.
